review_candidates.title: Director of Automation
review_candidates.location: San Salvador, San Salvador, El Salvador
review_candidates.description: Director of Automation Build the automation layer that allows AI to operate inside real companies. MAIC is building the enterprise architecture for AI. Enterprises already have data, systems, processes, applications, documents, and people performing thousands of interconnected actions every day. The challenge is turning all of that into an environment where AI can understand what is happening and safely take action. That is where the Automation team comes in. MAIC connects enterprise systems and operational data into a shared context layer. On top of that context, we build workflows, automations, applications, and AI agents that help organizations operate faster, more intelligently, and with less manual work. As Director of Automation, you will lead the team responsible for turning enterprise context into execution. You will own the strategy, architecture, standards, and delivery of automation across MAIC — from traditional RPA and APIs to AI agents, human-in-the-loop workflows, and intelligent enterprise automation. This is not a traditional RPA leadership role. We are building the infrastructure that allows AI to interact with real business systems safely and reliably. What you will own You will own MAIC’s automation function end-to-end. That includes: * Automation strategy and technical direction. * Architecture for enterprise automations and workflows. * RPA and browser automation. * API-based integrations and system actions. * AI-powered and agentic workflows. * Human-in-the-loop approval systems. * Production reliability and monitoring. * Reusable automation components and connectors. * Automation engineering standards. * Team development and technical leadership. * Delivery of customer automation projects. * Identification of new opportunities for automation across customer operations. You will be responsible for determining not only how a process should be automated, but also which technology should automate it. Sometimes the answer will be an API. Sometimes it will be RPA. Sometimes it will be an AI agent. Sometimes it will be a deterministic workflow with human approval. And often, it will be a combination of all four. What would your day look like? * Lead and grow a team of RPA, automation, and AI engineers. * Design the architecture for complex enterprise automation projects. * Review customer processes and identify opportunities for automation, AI augmentation, and process redesign. * Translate operational requirements into scalable technical solutions. * Decide when to use APIs, RPA, workflow engines, agents, or human-in-the-loop execution. * Architect automations that span multiple enterprise systems and data sources. * Build standards for production-grade automation across MAIC deployments. * Ensure automations are observable, auditable, recoverable, and secure. * Establish patterns for retries, queues, idempotency, exception handling, logging, monitoring, and escalation. * Oversee browser and desktop automations for legacy systems where modern APIs are unavailable. * Design AI-powered workflows that can interpret emails, documents, messages, forms, and unstructured information. * Define how AI agents interact with enterprise systems and what actions they are allowed to perform. * Design approval and control mechanisms for sensitive actions. * Work closely with MAIC’s Enterprise AI, Product, Data, and Engineering teams. * Connect automation workflows to MAIC’s ontology and enterprise context layer. * Create reusable actions, integrations, connectors, and automation components that can be deployed across customers. * Review technical designs and code produced by the automation engineering team. * Mentor engineers and establish strong engineering practices. * Participate directly in critical customer implementations. * Own the reliability and performance of automation running in production. * Continuously evaluate new automation and agentic technologies and determine where they fit within MAIC’s architecture. The kind of problems you will solve A traditional automation might say: When an invoice arrives, enter these fields into the ERP. At MAIC, the problem might look more like: An invoice arrives by email. MAIC identifies the supplier, connects the invoice to the corresponding purchase order, validates the amount against the order, checks whether the goods were received, detects a discrepancy, identifies the employee responsible for the purchase, retrieves the relevant communication history, and determines that approval is required. An AI agent prepares the recommended action. A human approves it. The automation executes the appropriate action across the ERP and other systems. Everything is logged and auditable. That is the type of automation architecture you will help build. What do you need to be successful? * 7+ years of experience in software engineering, automation, RPA, systems integration, enterprise technology, or related fields. * Experience leading engineers or technical delivery teams. * Strong hands-on understanding of RPA and enterprise automation. * Experience with tools such as UiPath, Power Automate, Automation Anywhere, Robocorp, Playwright, Selenium, or similar technologies. * Strong software engineering fundamentals. * Experience with Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#, Java, or similar languages. * Strong understanding of REST APIs, webhooks, authentication, databases, and enterprise integrations. * Experience designing integrations across complex enterprise systems. * Strong understanding of SQL and relational databases. * Experience designing distributed or asynchronous systems. * Understanding of queues, retries, idempotency, state management, and fault tolerance. * Experience operating automations or integrations in production environments. * Ability to design systems that are reliable, observable, secure, and maintainable. * Strong architectural judgment. * Ability to communicate effectively with both technical teams and business leaders. * Experience working directly with customers or enterprise stakeholders. * Ability to understand complex business processes and translate them into technical architectures. * Strong leadership, mentoring, and problem-solving skills. Strong pluses * Experience building AI agents or LLM-powered applications. * Experience with tool calling, MCP, or agent orchestration. * Experience with intelligent document processing. * Experience with OCR, computer vision, or multimodal AI. * Experience with process mining. * Experience with workflow orchestration platforms. * Experience integrating SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Salesforce, ServiceNow, or similar enterprise platforms. * Experience with event-driven architectures. * Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP. * Experience with Kubernetes, Docker, or distributed systems. * Experience designing human-in-the-loop systems. * Understanding of enterprise identity, RBAC, permissions, security, and audit trails. * Familiarity with knowledge graphs, ontologies, or enterprise semantic models. Leadership expectations This role is not only about managing a team. You should be able to go deep technically when necessary. You should be comfortable reviewing an architecture in the morning, debugging a failed production automation in the afternoon, working through a customer’s operational process with their leadership team, and then helping an engineer design a better implementation. You will establish the engineering culture of the Automation team. We expect you to: * Set a high technical bar. * Build systems for reuse rather than one-off scripts. * Push the team toward API-first automation where appropriate. * Know when RPA is the right tool and when it is not. * Design automations for failure, not just the happy path. * Treat monitoring and observability as part of the product. * Build security and permissions into the architecture. * Keep humans in control of sensitive decisions. * Help engineers grow technically and professionally. * Turn lessons from individual customer implementations into reusable MAIC platform capabilities. Why this role matters AI can generate an answer. Enterprise AI needs to do much more. It needs to understand the organization, know what actions are possible, respect permissions and business rules, interact with existing systems, recover when something fails, and know when a human needs to make the final decision. MAIC’s context layer gives AI an understanding of the enterprise. The Automation team gives it the ability to act. As Director of Automation, you will build and lead that capability. By being part of MAIC You will work on the intersection of enterprise software, AI, automation, and real-world operations. You will build systems that interact with the core infrastructure companies use every day. You will lead engineers working across traditional automation, enterprise integrations, intelligent workflows, and AI agents. And you will help define what automation looks like in a world where software no longer just follows predefined steps — it can understand context and participate intelligently in business processes. You will lead the team responsible for turning enterprise AI from intelligence into action.

review_candidates.title: Operations & Outreach Manager, Hawaii Mobile Museum of Tolerance
review_candidates.description: About Us Simon Wiesenthal Center (SWC) is a global Jewish human rights organization that confronts antisemitism and hate, defends the safety of Israel and Jews worldwide, and teaches the lessons of the Holocaust through awareness, advocacy, justice, education, and its Museums of Tolerance. With a constituency of over 400,000 member families since its founding in 1977, the SWC has an international footprint through its Museums of Tolerance, Moriah Films, and the Digital Terrorism + Hate Project. Headquartered in Los Angeles, it maintains operations in New York, Chicago, Miami, Toronto, Paris, Berlin, Jerusalem, and Buenos Aires. It is an accredited Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) at the United Nations, UNESCO, the Organization of American States, the Latin American Parliament, and the Council of Europe and maintains relationships with the highest levels of governments throughout the world. In 1993, the Center opened the Museum of Tolerance in Los Angeles to worldwide acclaim. The Museum has served as the Center’s flagship educational arm, challenging visitors to confront bigotry and racism, and to understand the Holocaust in both historical and contemporary contexts. In addition, the Center developed Moriah Media to produce theatrical documentaries to educate global audiences. Moriah has produced 17 documentaries to date, two of which have received the Academy Award for best feature documentary, The Long Way Home and Genocide. About The Mobile Museum Of Tolerance The Mobile Museum of Tolerance is a traveling educational experience that brings immersive programs on antisemitism, civil rights, media literacy, and civic responsibility directly to schools and communities. Through interactive technology, storytelling, and inquiry-based learning, MMOT programs help students explore questions of identity, bias, and democratic responsibility in the modern information environment. The Hawaiʻi Mobile Museum of Tolerance (HMMOT) expands this mission across the Hawaiian Islands, delivering programs in Holocaust education, media literacy, civic engagement, anti-bias education, and human rights education. The work will be done with deep awareness of and respect for the cultures of Native Hawaiians and the many ethnic groups that are well-established in Hawaii, as well as those that are recent arrivals. Through collaboration with local educators, cultural practitioners, schools, and community organizations, HMMOT seeks to deliver programming that is responsive to Hawaiʻi's unique cultural, historical, and educational landscape. HMMOT believes that Hawaii’s multiethnic mix, in which no one race predominates, offers a unique and powerful platform for anti-hatred and anti-discrimination work. Position Summary The Operations & Outreach Manager serves as the operational backbone of the Hawaiʻi Mobile Museum of Tolerance, ensuring the efficient scheduling, deployment, coordination, and utilization of HMMOT programming statewide. This position is responsible for managing school outreach logistics, program scheduling, logistics coordination, site preparation, stakeholder communications, and operational reporting. Working closely with the Program Manager, national MMOT leadership, MRA (bus contractor), bus drivers, facilitators, and community partners, the Operations & Outreach Manager helps ensure that every HMMOT engagement is executed with professionalism, efficiency, and a commitment to respectful, community-centered engagement. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, relationship-focused, and understands the importance of building trust through collaborative, culturally responsive, and place-based approaches to community engagement in Hawaiʻi. Essential Responsibilities Scheduling & Program Coordination: Serve as the primary coordinator for all HMMOT scheduling and booking activities across the Hawaiian Islands. Manage the statewide calendar and deployment schedule to maximize accessibility and program reach. Coordinate bookings with schools, districts, community organizations, and educational partners while ensuring clear communication and responsiveness. Maintain scheduling systems, operational databases, and program records with accuracy and attention to detail. Ensure timely communication regarding program confirmations, logistics, preparation requirements, and follow-up activities. Monitor program utilization and identify opportunities to expand access and participation statewide. Coordinate facilitator schedules and staffing assignments to support high-quality program delivery. Outreach & Relationship Management Build and maintain strong relationships with schools, educators, community organizations, and stakeholder groups throughout Hawaiʻi. Serve as a primary point of contact for program inquiries, scheduling requests, and outreach efforts. Conduct outreach that is grounded in respect, reciprocity, and meaningful relationship-building rather than transactional engagement. Support participation efforts across diverse communities while ensuring programming remains responsive to local needs and perspectives. Assist with community meetings, open houses, stakeholder briefings, and educational events. Foster ongoing communication with partners to support positive experiences, repeat engagement, and long-term collaboration. Engage with stakeholders in a manner that reflects Hawaiʻi's values of community partnership, mutual respect, and cultural awareness. Logistics & Operations Coordinate all logistical requirements necessary for successful HMMOT deployments. In collaboration with MRA, mobile operators and drivers, ensure site readiness, parking access, power requirements, participant flow, accessibility considerations, and operational needs are addressed in advance. Collaborate with fleet, facilities, and operations teams regarding vehicle scheduling, maintenance, and readiness. Coordinate transportation, lodging, and travel arrangements as needed. Manage inventory, educational materials, supplies, and program resources. Support event setup, execution, and breakdown while maintaining operational excellence and attention to participant experience. Assist in ensuring deployments are carried out in a manner that reflects respect for local communities, host sites, and cultural protocols when applicable. Data Management & Reporting Maintain accurate participation records, scheduling data, and operational documentation. Track student, educator, and community engagement metrics across all programming Manage CRM, scheduling, and reporting platforms to support operational effectiveness. Generate monthly, quarterly, and annual reports for leadership and stakeholders. Support grant reporting and data collection requirements. Monitor outreach pipelines, bookings, utilization rates, and participation trends to support strategic planning and continuous improvement. Community Engagement & Events Assist with planning and execution of: Community events Public programs Stakeholder briefings Funder visits Open houses Advisory committee meetings Represent HMMOT at educational gatherings, conferences, and community events throughout Hawaiʻi. Support storytelling, impact collection, and community visibility initiatives that are community-informed and reflective of local perspectives. Help cultivate partnerships that strengthen HMMOT's presence and impact across the islands. Administrative Support Prepare contracts, MOUs, confirmations, and program documentation. Track invoices, purchase requests, and operational expenses. Maintain organized digital and physical filing systems. Coordinate meetings, timelines, and project deliverables. Support compliance with organizational policies, grant requirements, and operational procedures. Qualifications Qualifications: MUST RESIDE IN HAWAII TO BE CONSIDERED Required Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience. Minimum of three years of experience in operations, project management, outreach, event coordination, nonprofit administration, education administration, or related fields. Exceptional organizational and project management skills. Strong customer service and relationship-building abilities. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously. Strong attention to detail and follow-through. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, CRM systems, and scheduling platforms. Valid driver's license and ability to travel throughout Hawaiʻi, including inter-island travel. Preferred Experience with logistics coordination, event management, or fleet operations. Experience managing databases, reporting systems, and program metrics. Experience working with K–12 schools, districts, or educational organizations. Experience in museum, nonprofit, or community-based programming. Familiarity with Hawaiʻi's educational landscape and communities. Understanding of Hawaiʻi's cultural, historical, and ethnic perspectives. Core Competencies Project Management Logistics Coordination Scheduling & Calendar Management Community Outreach Relationship Management Customer Service Excellence Operational Planning Communication Data Management & Reporting Problem Solving Attention to Detail Follows through reliably and honors commitments Ability to build successful collaborations Success Measures Within the first year, the Operations & Outreach Manager will: Establish and maintain a highly efficient statewide scheduling and deployment system with guidance available for best practices from previous MMOT launches. Achieve program utilization and outreach goals established by HMMOT leadership. Develop trusted relationships with schools, educators, and community partners across Hawaiʻi. Ensure smooth execution of all HMMOT deployments and events. Maintain accurate operational records and reporting systems. Support the successful launch and expansion of HMMOT programming statewide. Contribute to a culture of respect, collaboration, responsiveness, and community partnership throughout all operations. Closing Statement The Operations & Outreach Manager plays a critical role in ensuring that the Hawaiʻi Mobile Museum of Tolerance reaches communities across the islands with efficiency, excellence, and impact. This position supports the Simon Wiesenthal Center's mission to combat hate, strengthen civic understanding, and foster meaningful dialogue through education while honoring Hawaiʻi's communities, history, and cultural identity. Our Benefits We value our people and offer a collaborative and engaging culture. As a SWC employee, you will enjoy work/life balance, generous time off and comprehensive benefits and programs. The Simon Wiesenthal Center embraces inclusivity and values our diverse community. We are committed to building a team based on qualifications, merit, and business need. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
